Celebrating 10 years of Bishops Corner Café: A community staple

Carrie Moniot
August 3, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:18
Instaread

Editor’s note: This is the third in an ongoing series highlighting legacy businesses in our West Hills communities. What’s a legacy businesses? It’s a long-standing, community-oriented, independent business, often small, that is vital to a neighborhood’s identity, culture and economy.

If you’d like to nominate a legacy business in your neighborhood for consideration for a future installment, please drop us a line at mail@westhillsgazette.com.

Big changes are coming to the area around Bishops Corner Café in Robinson Township.

A substantial road improvement project that figures to take five years to complete will transform the landscape – and could cause headaches for those who operate businesses in the area.

But after a decade of serving loyal customers, chief proprietor Charley Larkin has no intention of closing his doors. Rather, Bishops is forging ahead despite the uncertainty.

The cozy café, which occupies a building that’s been in place for more than 70 years, celebrated its 10th anniversary on July 26.

Ribs and chicken were in the smoker, cocktails and beer were flowing and customers came from near and far, as the café held a parking lot barbecue to thank loyal customers for 10 years of support.

“Ten years is a huge accomplishment for any small business, especially in the bar and restaurant industry, where many don’t survive,” Larkin said.

“I think it’s a testament to how hard we work and have dedicated ourselves to serving the community.”

Bishops has gone through many phases over the years, yet the family-owned bar and restaurant maintains the flavor of a classic western Pennsylvania tavern -- a warm, friendly atmosphere where everybody knows your name.

Larkin’s mother, Kathryn, makes all the homemade soups, including turtle soup, a customer favorite. He credits his father, John, for seizing the opportunity to take over the bar when it became available, despite his and his mother’s reluctance.

“My mom and dad were proprietors of the Outlet Barn Garden Center right down the road, so we were patrons before we took the establishment over 10 years ago, and here we are 10 years later,” Larkin pointed out.

The building at 4701 Campbells Run Road was built in 1955 by the family of Larkin’s landlady Nancy Bishop, who died in 2024, just a few days after her 77th birthday.  It’s had a number of incarnations over the years: ice cream parlor, diner and now a bar and restaurant.

“We mean a lot to our regulars, but being situated in the airport corridor here, we have impressed many out-of-towners as well,” Larkin said.

Patty Meehan, who lives nearby, has been a loyal customer of Bishops Corner Cafe for a decade.

“This place is just so special," she said. "People come in from out of town and leave. When they come back to town, they come

right back to Bishops.”

“You come in as a patron, you leave as a friend.”

One thing that has remained constant is the building’s presence at the busy intersection of Campbells Run and Boyce roads in Robinson Township.

That places it right in the middle of the five-year $45.8 million reconstruction project underway along the 1.63-mile stretch of Campbells Run between McMichael Road and Keiners Lane.

Infrastructure upgrades and drainage improvements will be made, along with the widening and addition of turning lanes at key intersections and the realignment of Boyce Road and Parkway View Drive to create a new four-way intersection with traffic signals.

An average of 14,646 motorists use Campbells Run Road daily. The project, expected to be completed in 2031, is the largest ever undertaken by the Allegheny County Public Works Department.

More than 50 side streets and driveways between McMichael Road and Keiners Lane create bottlenecks on the existing two-lane road. County Public Works officials say the project will improve traffic flow and safety and point out the extended timeline should help reduce the impact on businesses and drivers.

Larkin worries that the construction project will cost him a portion of his already small parking lot.

“This whole area is going to look entirely different,” he said. “We’re existing in limbo at the moment. We don’t really know what the next 10 years hold here, after what we’ve painstakingly built here over the years.

“Right now, we’re just muddling through.”

The building is currently for sale, following Nancy Bishop’s passing. However, Larkin and his family are talking to her estate in an effort to keep the Bishops legacy alive for as long as they can.

Patrons like Meehan are hoping that's the case.

“Trust, love, friendship, family, conversation is all anyone wants," she said, "and we always have it at Bishops Corner Café.”

Larkin said the relationships that his business has built with its customers as a result of being a Robinson staple mean a great deal to him.

"I feel like we're a hidden gem here," said Larkin, who added that local "watering holes" like his are going by the wayside. amidst all the chains in the area.

“We’re kind of the last of a dying breed,” he said. “Despite how small we may be, we’re a mighty team and I’m proud of everything we’ve accomplished over these 10 years -- and I’m hoping we can continue it.”
